comment: Solar wind speeds have increased further overnight due to ongoing coronal hole effects, and are expected to remain elevated throughout the first forecast interval. A coronal mass ejection (CME) that left the Sun on 21 July has also been assessed to be partially Earth-directed. Whilst the bulk of the CME is expected to pass to the north, a glancing blow is possible late in the first forecast interval. ACTIVE periods of geomagnetic activity are likely during the first forecast interval, with a chance for STORM G1 periods, particularly if the CME does become geoeffective.
role: independent advisory; score_effect=0 until prospective validation
